quote.text: How much of my money is actually safe to spend

promise.text: How much money is safe to spend after your bills?

art.why: the carousel's topic: the moment and its guide name "money", "spend"

lines.text: Your balance is not what you can spend.
Take off the bills still due and the money you are holding back, in five steps, and one number is left.

eyebrow.text: Work out your own number in five steps

head.text: Open the account you pay bills from and write down the available balance, not the current one.

eyebrow.text: Work out your own number in five steps

head.text: Write down your next payday, then list every bill, subscription and card payment that leaves before it.

eyebrow.text: Work out your own number in five steps

body.text: If you pay a credit card in full, that card's balance is a bill too.
If you carry a balance, subtract the payment you'll actually make.

eyebrow.text: Work out your own number in five steps

head.text: Subtract what you're holding back: tax money, a deposit, the cushion you don't want to touch.

body.text: Then subtract anything you've committed to but not paid, like a booking or a repair.

eyebrow.text: Work out your own number in five steps

head.text: Write the result at the top of a note and date it.

body.text: If you want a weekly figure, divide by the weeks left.
Next time you're about to spend, look at that number first, then look at the balance.

line.text: One figure, updated as the cycle goes on, with every number that feeds it shown line by line if you want to check the working.
